steps.text: Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed pot; add flour and stir gently until blended, being careful not to let it brown. Gradually add milk, stirring constantly, then stir in half-and-half until smooth. Add corn and green onions; cook until tender, about a few minutes.

Add crabmeat, pepper, salt, and soy sauce; simmer until heated through and small bubbles form around the edges—do not let boil. Adjust seasonings to taste. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Crabmeat and Corn Soup
raw_recipe.description: A rich chowder made with white kernel corn, fresh cracked crab meat, and green onions in a soup base of whole milk and half-and-half.
raw_recipe.name: Crabmeat and Corn Soup

review.reviewBody: I found this recipe less than one half hour ago and dinner is on the table. Added a splash of hot sauce and sherry. I cannot believe how quick and easy this was to prepare with canned crab meat and white corn. Everyone is very, very impressed. Make this and enjoy.

A really tasty and simple chowder. Had some doubts about adding the soy sauce. Sampled it in a small bowl first. Oh my gosh! The soy sauce made all the difference in the great taste. Will make this for many years to come.

I had some heavy cream, salt pork and cobbed corn to use up, and found this recipe. Even my picky 5 year old ate some. I also made some changes: I sauteed onions and garlic after cooking the salt pork. I also used 1 c heavy cream, 2 c 1% milk and 2 c seafood stock, and about 3 potatoes (what kept my 5 year old from having more). I used leftover corn from the cob, and canned crab meat. Finally, I didn't add the soy sause right away, but I agree with another poster: try it - it makes the dish! You bet I'll be making this again.

I give it 4 stars because I changed it up a bit. The soy sauce seemed odd, but I gave it a chance, and it worked beautifully.

I made an andouille and corn/veggie stock, reduced down to 1 cup, which I used as part of the liquid. The change was 1 cup of stock, 2 cups of heavy cream, and 1 cup of whole milk. 

I also changed it to include 1 can of lump crab (around 6 oz) and 1 pound of raw jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined, poached to par-cook level in the stock, and then halved sideways, finishing the cooking in the chowder right before adding the crab. If you poach the shrimp until pink only, then it'll take 8-10 minutes to finish the cooking, at which time the crab meat is added and it's simmered as stated in the recipe. 

I used about 1/4 cup of dried parsley flakes in lieu of the fresh parsley, and I reduced the amount of green onion in the finished product to 1/4 cup.

Otherwise, as stated! Great recipe.

Killer quick crab recipe!
I made 1/2 the recipe and made some changes. 
Had some fresh dungeness to use. 
Softened 1/4 white onion, Boiled 2 small potatoes, and celery. 
Made the roux, and added about 10oz heavy cream, and some whole milk. More fat more flavor! Added in the almost cooked potatoes , celery, and 3/4 can of corn kernels, and onion. I omitted the corn juice, cause that sounded gross to me. I added to taste garlic powder, old bay, celery salt, onion powder, white pepper, black pepper, sea salt, a dash of dill, and some old bay. Brought that almost to a boil for about 2 minutes, then added the crab, and a little extra soy sauce. I also adjusted the whole milk to suit the thickness of the soup we like, which is chowder, so nice and thick. I served it with fresh sourdough bread. 
This was a super hit with my hubby, who is very picky. Will definitely make again. Thank you!

People think because I'm a chef, that I like recipes that have a ton of ingredient, have 1000 steps and take all day to make. NOPE! I like delicious and easy, and this recipe fits the bill. I has a bunch of odds and ends and this used them all up. I used 1 can of creamed corn, about 1/2 cup of frozen kernels and some left over baby corn from stir fry. My boyfriend isn't much of a seafood eater so I figured I would have to doctor this up for him to eat it. I add 1 Lg red bell pepper (small dice) and 1/2 lb of red and gold baby potatoes (quartered and microwaved till done). Out of soy so replaced with Worcestershire. topped with mix of cilantro and Italian parsley because that is what I cut this morning. OMG so good. Eating it while I write this. I think the potatoes give it that chowder texture and stretch what could be a pricey dish. FYI, potatoes absorb salt so your soup may taste different after sitting. How about topping with some hot crisp bacon?

I've made this recipe multiple times and my family, including 2 teens??it. I followed the recipe exactly as written and made 2 modifications every other time, which improved the flavor. Replace white pepper with cracked black pepper, add 1-2 Tbsp finely chopped red pepper and add either minced garlic or garlic powder at 1st step.

Wonderful! A local deli makes a spicy crab and corn chowder that is just devine, but it has 31 grams of fat. I've been looking for a recipe to satisfy my love of that chowder that's easier on the waistline and this is it! Changes I made: 2Tbs butter + 2 Tbs margarine (ran out of butter) Skim milk instead of whole Fat free half-and-half 1/2 cup chopped green onions (got tired of chopping) 1 cup Mexicorn + 1 cup frozen corn (wanted a touch of red & green peppers) Added 1/8 tsp cayenne pepper (for a little kick) Added 1/2 tsp parsley flakes I sauteed my corn and green onions before starting anything else and set aside to add later. I used a 16oz. tub of claw crab meat. This was sooooo good! Even my 10 year old who is certain she does NOT like crab not only ate it quickly, but used her bread to scoop up the last little bit in the bowl. I didn't tell her it was crab meat and she thought it was excellent. I think the next time, I will add 1/2 to 1tsp Old Bay. I was out and didn't realize it. Great recipe! Thanks for sharing!

This was delicious! I used left over king crab and lobster with fresh corn and 1.5 potatoes. I sautéed the onion with garlic and butter before adding and cooked the potatoes beforehand as well. I also added some hot sauce. It is so thick and creamy and the soy sauce Rocks this dish! Yummy!

Good flavor. Heartier than expected. I served in bread bowls and cubed and toasted the bread that I hollowed out of the bowls in olive oil and sprinkled with rosemary and thyme. I spooned the chowder into the bowls, topped with a little shaving of swiss cheese, and a few of the homemade croutons.

This is amazing!!! Since I had yellow onion instead of green, I took several reviewers' suggestion to soften it in the butter before adding the flour. I used skim milk instead of whole, along with the half and half, and we thought it was still plenty rich. Then for the crab-- crabstick. Finally, since my husband is a native Baltimoron, of course I had to add a generous amount of Old Bay. So easy, quick, and delicious--this one is going into our fast rotation!
Added some chicken broth and a tsp of old bay. also used heavy cream but a great recipe
Made this soup several times. Works fine with fat-free milk instead of whole milk. I add in 1 tsp worcestershire and 1 tsp hot sauce.

This was delightful! Next time, I might try some potatoes to thicken it just a touch, but otherwise, it was fantastic.

The only substantive change I made was adding a few splashes of Thai fish sauce. I did use regular onions instead of green, but it still worked!

We really loved this recipe. I made just a couple small changes. Instead of green onions, I sauteed half a sweet onion chopped in the butter at the beginning of the recipe and I added a good tablespoon of Old Bay with the seasonings.
I decided on going with both fresh and imitation crab meat. Awesomely delicious thankyou for sharing!!
Really simple and good tasting chowder. I used imitation crab and it was still very good. Great on a cold windy day.
yummmm! used a can of corn, and combination of imitation crab and a can of crab meat - was delicious!!
Big hit with the family. I also added some boiled diced potatoes for substance and Old Bay Seasoning. It's so easy and very tasty.
This soup is delicious! Making a double batch and having the family over. I know they’re going to love it.
